free_tier.stated: No storage and no relayed bandwidth: Trystero borrows an existing decentralised network purely to exchange WebRTC SDP offers.

egress.terms: Data flows peer-to-peer via WebRTC; the signalling network never sees the payload. The operator's cost is SDP messages only.

record.chaining: The cleanest signalling example: because only SDP crosses the third party, there is no bandwidth quota to hit and no operator who could impose one. Note the caveat that WebRTC needs a TURN relay when both peers are behind symmetric NAT. That is where real relaying cost reappears, and Trystero does not supply it.
record.limits_note: Signalling only. Browser WebRTC connection-count limits force a room/namespace design.
record.reliability_note: No TURN service included; symmetric-NAT pairs will fail to connect rather than fall back.

evidence.proved: 'To establish a direct peer-to-peer connection with WebRTC, a signalling channel is needed to exchange peer information (SDP). Typically this involves running your own matchmaking server but Trystero abstracts this away'; strategies listed: BitTorrent, Nostr, MQTT, Supabase, Firebase, IPFS, self-hosted WebSocket relay
'Use our free cloud server or host your own PeerServer' (free signalling broker; relayed data still needs a TURN server)
